subject: research/buildbot-carrycop
professional: a humanoid-robotics controls researcher (LIPM/ZMP gait, whole-body torque limits) reviewing for ICRA/Humanoids; first check would be whether the planned-CoP offset is actually what the scorer sees, whether the actuator limits are datasheet values, and whether a one-grid-cell result is outside discretisation noise

evidence.correctness: Ran with /usr/bin/python3.13 (mujoco 4.0.0 via pyenv.py). (1) Re-ran 7 scored cases through experiments/run.py job() (G1 4 kg c=-6 cm L0.2 T1.5; G1 4 kg c=0; G1 0 kg; G1 3 kg c=+3 cm; H1 0 kg c=-3; H1 10 kg; G1 5 kg): ok flags and torque ratios match stored results.json to 4 decimals (one 0.9677 vs 0.9679, a numerics difference). (2) Re-ran the full G1 4 kg slice (6 offsets x 36 gaits, 216 cases): best speeds 0.133, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, none and passing counts match results.json. (3) Recounted README headline from results.json: passing per offset G1 32,34,38,36,20,0 and H1 0,6,8,6,0,0 (exact); G1 torque ratio>1 cases per offset 125 to 151 (README 125 to 150, 151 at 9 cm, trivial); CoP-off-sole 114 to 180 (exact); H1 IK residual>5e-3 cases 73 to 87 (exact). (4) Orbit recomputed independently by RK4 shooting (no closed form): constant c=-6 cm mid-step x=-0.052785 vs model -0.052785; linear ramp -6>6 cm mid-step x=0 vs model 0 (to 1e-12). (5) results.txt table regenerates from results.json. Not rerun: the full 1,944 and 1,440 case sweeps (about 40 and 30 min).
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: closed-form orbit with CoP offset (works, tests); 1,944-case sweep for G1 and H1 over six offsets (results.json has exactly 1,944 rows); ramp follow-up (results_ramp.json/txt present, 1,440 cases per README, table values match README text); figure.png exists; project.json card present. Not done and stated as not done: time-varying ZMP preview, trunk and arm motion, learned policy, falls. No stubs or TODOs found. The README's own claim 'the earlier note that trunk compensation would raise the ceiling is not supported' is bounded to this one-parameter version.
evidence.verification: pytest -q tests: 10 passed in 0.23 s (README says 6, stale). The tests are of the closed-form orbit only: endpoints, equation of motion by finite differences, offset 0 equals carryphase, ramp reduces to constant. Mutations: (M1) A = -L/2 + c in lipm_x_cop: 3 tests failed, caught. (M2) ramp term (c1-c0)*t/T*0.5: 3 failed, caught. (M3) flipped the sign of the offset passed from cop_offset() to lipm_x_cop (the wiring into buildbot_carryphase): all 10 passed, NOT caught. There is no test that cop_offset/score/cop_ramp actually feed the orbit into C.score, nor of run.py's best()/table logic, nor any regression test on a stored result. The headline is therefore only protected by re-running the 40-minute sweep, which no CI does.
evidence.craft: Read src/buildbot_carrycop/model.py (68 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, run_ramp.py, figure.py, pyproject.toml. Clean, small, documented, reuses carryphase unchanged. Defects: cop_offset monkeypatches module global C.lipm_x with try/finally (not thread-safe, fragile if carryphase imports the name elsewhere; the Pool uses processes so the sweep is fine); no validation of sinh(T/Tc)=0 or non-positive T; pyproject pythonpath hard-codes sibling projects (no declared dependency on buildbot-carryphase); sys.path hacking in run.py; best() tie-break picks lowest ratio silently; unused imports (sys, Path) in tests.
evidence.claims: Each headline number traced to results.json/results.txt (see correctness) and holds. Disclaimers present: simulated, preliminary, not a safety case (ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066, OSHA), limitations list. Cites Kajita 2001 and 2003. Defects: '6 tests' stale (10); 'waist pitch, as in carryphase' is the binding joint is true only to 3 cm, at +6 and +9 cm the ankle pitch is the most frequent worst joint (results.json worst counts: ankle 84 and 136 vs waist 72 and 44); 'deterministic' holds on this box (spot cases match) but is not tested across mujoco builds, and a sibling audit (buildbot-carry) found a headline that did not reproduce under another build. 'Torque is the wall' is a count of ratio>1 cases, which overlaps with the CoP-outside-sole count (the same case can fail both), so the two numbers are not shares of a total.
evidence.fitness: As research: it answers a narrow question honestly with a negative result (a constant or linear planned CoP offset moves the best speed by one grid cell). A researcher can reuse lipm_x_ramp and the harness. Weaknesses: the headline gain (0.10 to 0.13 m/s) is one cell on a coarse 6x6 grid with 2 to 3 mm CoP margins at the best cases, no sensitivity to torque limits (peak values from the vendor model), no step-width or hand-pose sweep, no uncertainty; a negative result on a prescribed-gait model says little about what a real controller can do, as the README itself says. Not publishable on its own; it is a programme note.
evidence.domain: Compared with Kajita et al. 2001 (3D-LIPM) and 2003 (preview control): the shifted-CoP LIPM x''=(g/z)(x-c) is textbook and correct, and a linear c(t) closed form is right. Departures a gait researcher would flag: the offset is applied to the planned COM orbit only, the scored CoP comes from inverse dynamics of a rigid prescribed motion, so 'planning the CoP' is not closed-loop ZMP control and cannot use trunk momentum; constant height z; zero double support and no impact (so no real step cycle); a point-mass load; vendor peak torques used as continuous limits (thermal and bandwidth ignored); no foot compliance. Fine as a screening study, short of what a humanoid-locomotion reviewer would accept as evidence about carrying capacity.

defects.what: Tests never exercise the wiring from cop_offset/cop_ramp into buildbot_carryphase.score; flipping the sign of the offset passes all 10 tests, so the headline sweep is guarded only by a 40-minute manual rerun.
Headline gain is a single grid cell (0.10 to 0.13 m/s) at CoP margins of a few mm with no sensitivity analysis on grid or torque limits.
Waist pitch is called the binding joint at every offset; at +6 and +9 cm the ankle pitch is the most frequent worst joint.
Monkeypatching a module global (C.lipm_x) for the orbit swap; no input validation; hard-coded sibling pythonpath.

verdict: A small, honest negative-result study built on buildbot-carryphase. Every headline count I rechecked (passing per offset, torque and IK failure ranges, G1 4 kg row, seven spot cases, a 216-case slice) reproduces from the code and results.json, and the orbit matches an independent RK4 integration. It is held back by weak guards and thin science: the tests cover only the closed-form orbit (a sign flip in the offset wiring survived all tests), the one positive finding is a single grid cell with mm-level margins and no sensitivity, and the model (prescribed gait, orbit-only CoP, no controller) cannot answer what a gait-control reviewer would care about. Correctness and claims meet the bar; verification does not, so the subject does not meet the bar overall.
